title: ACET Regional Integration Graduate Intern 2026: Fully Funded Career Opportunity in Economic Research and African Development
summary: The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is inviting applications for a Regional Integration (RI) Graduate Intern to support research, policy development, regional coordination, stakeholder engagement, and program implementation. This opportunity is particularly relevant for recent postgraduate graduates who want to build professional experience in economic research, regional integration, international development, public policy, data analysis, and African economic transformation . The position is based in Accra, Ghana, with remote work arrangements available , and the successful intern will work under the supervision of a Senior Policy Analyst within ACET s Regional Integration Program. Applications are open until Thursday, 27 August 2026 . Opportunity Overview Organization: African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) Opportunity: Regional Integration Graduate Intern Job Title: Graduate Intern – Regional Integration (RI) Category: Internship Location: Accra / Remote Posted: 13 August 2026 Reporting to: Senior Policy Analyst Application deadline: Thursday, 27 August 2026 Application method: Email application Application email: pnc@acetforafrica.org Interview format: Virtual or in person for candidates based in Ghana Target applicants: Recent postgraduate graduates, particularly those with backgrounds in Economics or related Social Sciences About the African Center for Economic Transformation The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is an African economic policy institute focused on supporting Africa s long-term economic transformation. The organization conducts research, provides policy advice, and works to encourage practical action that can help African countries develop stronger economies, reduce poverty, and improve livelihoods. ACET describes itself as an organization focused on advancing African solutions to African challenges . Its work brings together research, policy thinking, partnerships, and practical approaches to economic transformation across the continent. For an aspiring policy professional, researcher, development practitioner, economist, or analyst, an internship with an institution such as ACET can provide exposure to the intersection of research, public policy, economic development, regional cooperation, and government engagement . About the Regional Integration Program The internship is situated within ACET s Regional Integration (RI) Program . Regional integration is an important component of Africa s economic development agenda. It involves strengthening economic relationships between African countries, improving cross-border trade and cooperation, supporting regional value chains, and identifying policies that can help countries participate more effectively in regional and continental markets. The intern will therefore have the opportunity to contribute to work connected to regional value chain development , while gaining exposure to research, program coordination, stakeholder engagement, partnerships, reporting, and business development. Role and Purpose of the Internship The Regional Integration Program is looking for a graduate intern who can provide support across several areas of its work. The role is designed around three broad areas: Research and analysis Program coordination and implementation Stakeholder engagement The intern will also contribute to communications and knowledge products, business development activities, and administrative support when required. This makes the opportunity broader than a traditional research internship. The successful candidate is expected to combine analytical ability, strong writing, organizational skills, communication skills, and the ability to work effectively with different stakeholders . Key Responsibilities 1. Research and Data Analysis A major component of the position involves supporting ACET s research activities. The intern will assist project teams with: Collecting relevant research data. Organizing and analyzing information. Interpreting data. Synthesizing research findings. Providing inputs into research reports. Supporting evidence-based analysis. Contributing to the development of research outputs. This responsibility makes research ability particularly important for applicants. Candidates should be comfortable working with information from different sources, identifying relevant evidence, understanding findings, and communicating analytical conclusions clearly. 2. Cross-Country Project Coordination The intern will support coordination across projects involving different countries and stakeholders. Responsibilities may include: Supporting communication between project teams. Helping coordinate activities across countries. Assisting with project-related follow-up. Engaging stakeholders during research validation processes. Supporting dissemination of research findings. Helping ensure project activities progress according to established plans. This aspect of the role could provide valuable experience for candidates interested in project management, international development, policy coordination, consulting, and regional development . 3. Policy Briefs, Blogs and Thought Pieces The successful candidate will also support the program s communications and knowledge-sharing activities. This includes working with the program Lead to develop: Thought pieces. Policy briefs. Blogs. Research narratives. Key messages related to regional integration. The objective is to make complex research and policy findings easier for policymakers and other stakeholders to understand and use. Strong writing skills will therefore be important. Applicants should be able to take research information, identify the most important findings, and communicate those findings in a clear and accessible way. 4. Business Development Support The intern may also contribute to ACET s business development activities. This could involve conducting background research to support the preparation of technical proposals . Candidates interested in consulting, development organizations, research institutes, policy institutions, or international organizations may find this aspect of the role particularly valuable because it provides exposure to how organizations develop proposals around technical and policy projects. 5. Administrative Support The intern will provide additional administrative support to the Regional Integration Program when required. This may involve helping with coordination, documentation, communication, scheduling, reporting, research organization, and other activities necessary for effective program implementation. The role therefore requires someone who is not only academically capable but also organized, dependable, adaptable, and comfortable handling multiple responsibilities . Educational Requirements Applicants should have a minimum of a postgraduate degree in Economics or a related field in the Social Sciences . Relevant academic backgrounds may include areas such as: Economics Development Economics International Development Public Policy Political Science International Relations Development Studies Public Administration Other closely related Social Science disciplines However, applicants should carefully assess whether their postgraduate qualification is sufficiently related to the role before applying. Professional and Relevant Experience Previous professional experience is not presented as an absolute requirement, but relevant experience will strengthen an application. ACET specifically indicates that experience gained through: Employment Volunteering Internships Research International development activities Economic research Related development work can be an advantage. The internship is intended for recent graduates who are looking to gain practical experience and transition into the world of work . Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their academic background, research projects, internships, volunteer work, employment, or other experiences have prepared them to contribute to the Regional Integration Program. Required Skills and Abilities Excellent Research Skills Research is central to this internship. Applicants should be able to: Find and evaluate relevant information. Conduct structured research. Organize evidence. Analyze information. Draw meaningful conclusions. Contribute to research reports. Data Analysis Skills The position also requires candidates who can support data collection and analysis. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to work with data and translate information into useful findings. Where applicable, candidates should highlight relevant coursework, research projects, professional assignments, or technical tools they have used for data analysis. Strong Writing Skills Writing is another major requirement. The intern may contribute to: Research reports Policy briefs Blogs Thought pieces Technical proposals Research summaries Applicants should therefore ensure that their CV and cover letter demonstrate clear, professional, analytical writing. French Language Skills ACET states that candidates should possess a good working knowledge of French . This is an important requirement because the position involves regional and cross-country work. Applicants who have French-language qualifications, professional experience using French, academic exposure to French, or practical communication ability should clearly indicate this in their application. Teamwork The intern will work with project teams and interact with colleagues and stakeholders. Applicants should therefore demonstrate the ability to: Collaborate effectively. Contribute to team projects. Communicate professionally. Support colleagues. Work across different assignments. Ability to Work With Limited Oversight The organization is also looking for candidates who can work comfortably with limited supervision. This means applicants should demonstrate: Initiative Self-management Accountability Time management Problem-solving The ability to complete assigned tasks independently Personal Qualities ACET Is Looking For Beyond academic qualifications and technical skills, ACET highlights several personal qualities. Interpersonal Skills The successful candidate should have outstanding interpersonal skills and be able to communicate effectively with different people. Organizational Skills Because the position combines research, coordination, stakeholder engagement, communications, business development, and administrative responsibilities, strong organization will be essential. Communication Skills The intern will interact with colleagues, partners, government officials, and stakeholders from different backgrounds and cultures. Professional verbal and written communication will therefore be important. Administrative Ability Candidates should also be capable of handling administrative responsibilities efficiently and professionally. ACET s Core Values Applicants should understand the values of the organization before applying. ACET identifies five core values: Pioneering ACET seeks to push boundaries and operate in the spirit of a think and do tank. Respect The organization emphasizes mutual respect and believes that people grow by respecting one another. Integrity Transparency and accountability are central to ACET s approach. Collaboration ACET believes that strong results are achieved when people work effectively together. Excellence The organization strives for high standards of critical thinking and seeks effective solutions to difficult challenges. A strong cover letter should ideally show how the applicant s own experience and working style align with these values. Who Should Apply? This internship is particularly suited to recent postgraduate graduates who want to build professional experience in economic research, regional integration, public policy, international development, or related fields. Potentially relevant applicants include graduates with postgraduate qualifications in: Economics Development Economics Development Studies Political Science International Relations Public Policy Public Administration Other related Social Sciences Applicants with relevant research, internship, volunteer, or professional experience may have an additional advantage. The opportunity may also appeal to people seeking to build careers as: Policy analysts Economic researchers Development professionals Research analysts Project coordinators International development practitioners Public policy professionals Regional integration specialists Management or development consultants Countries and Geographic Eligibility The vacancy does not state a nationality restriction . The position is listed as Accra/Remote , and ACET describes itself as a Pan-African organization with a diversified African and global talent base. Candidates should therefore focus primarily on meeting the stated educational, professional, language, research, analytical, and interpersonal requirements. Candidates based in Ghana should note that interviews may be conducted in person , while virtual interviews may also be used. Because the vacancy does not explicitly specify a list of eligible countries or a nationality requirement, applicants outside Ghana should confirm their ability to participate remotely and their eligibility before submitting an application. Is This an Internship, Job, Scholarship or Fellowship? Category: Internship This is a graduate internship opportunity , not a scholarship, conference, award, competition, fellowship, grant, or permanent employment position. ACET explicitly notes that the internship does not guarantee employment after the internship . Applicants should therefore view the opportunity primarily as a professional development and experience-building opportunity. What Can Applicants Gain From the Opportunity? Although the vacancy does not advertise a specific financial benefit or salary package, the responsibilities indicate several potentially valuable professional development opportunities. Research Experience Participants can gain practical exposure to economic and policy research, including data collection, analysis, interpretation, and report development. Policy Writing Experience The intern can contribute to policy briefs, blogs, thought pieces, and other research communications. Regional Development Exposure Working within the Regional Integration Program can expose the intern to issues involving African economic integration and regional value chains. Cross-Country Coordination The role provides exposure to projects involving multiple countries and stakeholders. Stakeholder Engagement The intern may interact with partners, policymakers, government officials, and other stakeholders. Business Development The position also offers exposure to technical proposal development and background research for business development activities. Professional Networking Working within a Pan-African policy institution can provide opportunities to develop professional relationships with researchers, policy professionals, development practitioners, government stakeholders, and other experts. How to Apply Interested applicants are required to submit: A current CV A cover letter explaining why they are the most suitable candidate Applications should be submitted by email to: pnc@acetforafrica.org Applicants should ensure that their CV and cover letter are tailored specifically to the Regional Integration Graduate Intern position. More information about this internship, visit ACET for Africa For more global internship programs visit the OFY Website HERE How to Make Your Application Stronger Tailor Your CV Do not submit a generic CV if you can avoid it. Highlight experiences related to: Research Data analysis Policy Economics Development Regional integration Project coordination Stakeholder engagement Writing Administration Demonstrate Research Ability If you have completed a dissertation, thesis, research project, policy paper, academic publication, or professional research assignment, consider highlighting it. Highlight French Proficiency Because French is specifically identified as a desired skill, clearly state your level of French proficiency if applicable. Connect Your Experience to Regional Integration Your cover letter should explain why you are interested in regional integration and African economic transformation rather than simply stating that you need an internship.
